planting.note: Pot into a humid terrarium or cloche in spring using a light, evenly moist, well-drained mix; this Brazilian rainforest-floor species needs constant high humidity and will not tolerate dry indoor air.

directions: Grow in deep, bright-indirect shade with no direct sun, which scorches the leaves, in a terrarium or cloche where constant high humidity is easy to maintain. Native to the Brazilian rainforest floor, this low rosette-forming jewel plant carries olive-green, velvety leaves banded in silvery pink, making it a classic specialty houseplant for closed-case terrarium displays. Keep the soil evenly moist but never waterlogged, and avoid cold drafts or temperatures below 60°F. It has no outdoor frost tolerance and is grown strictly as an indoor terrarium plant outside the tropics.

planting.note: Pot into a humid terrarium in spring using a light, moisture-retentive mix; keep water off the foliage and avoid cold drafts, which this Javanese forest-floor species cannot tolerate.

directions: Grow in deep shade with very high humidity and warm, steady temperatures, the same closed-terrarium conditions that made this species a Victorian-era conservatory staple. Native to Java and Malaysia, pearl sonerila forms a compact mounding herb with dark green leaves stippled in silvery-pink 'pearl' spots. Keep the growing medium consistently moist without waterlogging, and water at the soil line rather than overhead to avoid fungal spotting on the velvety foliage. It has no cold tolerance and is grown exclusively as an indoor terrarium or vivarium plant outside equatorial climates.
sources: International Carnivorous Plant Society forums (terrarium plant culture notes)

planting.note: Divide and press cuttings into a humid terrarium's moist substrate in spring; this creeping groundcover roots readily along its stems and spreads to fill a vivarium floor.

directions: Grow in deep shade with high humidity and constant light moisture, mimicking the Southeast Asian forest floor it carpets in the wild. This low, creeping Urticaceae groundcover forms a dense mat of small rounded leaves only 1-2 inches tall, rooting at the nodes as it spreads, which makes it a favorite living groundcover for closed terrariums and bioactive vivariums. It has no tolerance for dry air or cold temperatures and should be treated strictly as an enclosed-habitat plant. Trim back overgrown runners periodically to keep the mat tidy and encourage dense new growth.

planting.note: Mount on bark or pot into a free-draining epiphyte mix of orchid bark and sphagnum in spring; let it dry between waterings as it would on a host tree in the wild.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial shade in a free-draining epiphyte mix, letting the roots dry out between waterings exactly as they would clinging to a host tree in the wild Philippine forest. Bagpipe plant is a trailing ant-plant epiphyte whose leaves inflate into distinctive hollow pouches that house symbiotic ants in nature, giving the species its common name. Mount it on bark or a hanging basket where the trailing stems can cascade, and avoid letting the roots sit in standing water. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a warm, humid greenhouse or indoor specialty plant outside the tropics.

planting.note: Pot into a free-draining epiphyte mix or mount on bark in spring; let dry between waterings, the same low-moisture culture used for other trailing Dischidia species.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial shade in a very free-draining epiphyte mix, letting the small fleshy leaves dry between waterings as this trailing vine would experience as an epiphyte in its native habitat. The small, oval, succulent-textured foliage strings along wiry trailing stems, making it a popular hanging-basket companion to the better-known string-of-hearts and other trailing Dischidia species. Avoid overwatering, which quickly rots the shallow epiphytic roots, and provide warm, humid conditions year-round. It has no frost tolerance outside the tropics.

planting.note: Root cuttings or divide established mats in spring into moist, humid terrarium or bedding soil; this close relative of Red Ivy (Hemigraphis alternata) shares the same easy, fast-rooting culture.

directions: Grow in shade to partial shade in consistently moist, humid conditions; metal leaf plant is a Southeast Asian relative of the more widely grown Red Ivy (Hemigraphis alternata), sharing its easy, fast-spreading creeping habit but carrying distinct metallic purple-bronze foliage. Use it as a low groundcover in a shaded terrarium, humid greenhouse bench, or as a seasonal bedding accent in frost-free climates. It roots readily from stem cuttings pressed directly into moist soil, making it simple to propagate and share. It has no tolerance for frost or dry indoor air for extended periods.

planting.note: Mount young plants on bark, cork, or a moss pole in spring so the juvenile stems can press flat and climb; keep humidity high and the growing medium evenly moist but never soggy.

directions: Grow in partial to full shade with high humidity and an evenly moist, well-drained substrate, mounting young plants on bark or a moss pole so the climbing stems can attach. Shingle plant is a Caribbean and Central American climbing epiphyte prized for its distinctive juvenile growth habit, pressing flat, overlapping leaves tightly against its support in a shingled pattern before shifting to a different leaf form as a mature climbing vine. It is a niche collector's plant with thinner nursery availability than more common terrarium species, so expect to source it from a specialty epiphyte or aroid vendor rather than a general houseplant retailer. Keep it out of direct sun and cold drafts, as it has no frost tolerance.
